cause: Long sequential FP32 accumulation differs from the parallel library accumulation; both GPU results are closer to the independent higher-precision reference.
proposed_fix: If the unchanged sequential-C gate remains required, supply and import an order-preserving reduction reference/backend. This will sacrifice parallel reduction performance. A higher-precision oracle is useful separate evidence, not a reason to relabel this strict failure.

cause: The extracted C initializes output to positive zero and adds the product. Native at::outer_out directly multiplies, preserving negative zero. Under the existing sign-sensitive gate these differ even though all finite numerical values agree.
proposed_fix: Keep the direct native outer result as a failed semantic comparison. To match the extracted C exactly, a separate actual-ATen baseline must implement the same zero-initialize then addition, with that changed baseline scope explicitly documented. Do not normalize zeros or silently change the source/gate.

cause: Raised/native outputs are bit-identical, but differ from sequential C. Exact-integer accumulation diagnoses the rounding error without changing the gate. All supported legacy FP32/FMA cuDNN backward-filter algorithms were tested and none passed the existing C gate.
proposed_fix: Keep the strict failure. No tested supported FP32/FMA algorithm meets the existing C/native contract. Exact sequential-C reproduction requires an order-preserving fallback; changing to a mathematical-error or native-equivalence contract requires an explicit methodological decision, not a silent tolerance change.
